To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the tryptophane side chain oxidase (TSO) is a new tool for reducing serotonin (5-HT) levels in the brain.
the hemoprotein TSOI transiently reduces brain 5HT levels in rats, abolishes sleep ⁄ wake rhythmicity and has no meaningful influences of total sleep amount.
TSOI injection rapidly reduces brain 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT) levels in rats without reducing other monoaminergic systems and without altering the circadian rhythm of core body temperature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how 5-HT signaling is involved in sleep regulation.
the mechanisms of sleep regulation, and in particular with the role of 1-tryptophan, a precursor of the sleep hormone melatonin, in the regulation of the sleep cycle
how the brain regulates sleep and wakefulness.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
5-HT is not necessary for normal sleep, but that it is important for the normal regulation of the sleep⁄wake rhythm.

TSOI injection reduces brain and peripheral 3-5-HT concentrations, and that these changes have no cumulative effect on daily sleep amount, but that they do abolish the sleep–wake cycle and have no effect on the circadian temperature rhythm.
the sleep regulatory properties of 5-HT are not a direct consequence of the sleep regulatory properties but rather a consequence of the sleep regulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 5-HT system is a key regulator of the sleep–wake cycle.
the role of 3-hydroxykynurenine is not limited to its function as an intermediate metabolite, but that it is an important regulator of sleep–wake rhythm.
5-HT signaling has a role in the regulation of the sleep-wake rhythm and circadian timing, but the specific mechanisms are not well understood.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TSOI injection is an effective method for transiently reducing brain 5HT levels without collateral influences on catecholeamine signaling.
the role of  5-HT signaling may not be limited to its well-described regulatory effects on circadian rhythm, but may have more specific effects on the sleep ⁿ wake rhythm.
the 5-HT depletion by TSOI is rapid, reversible, and specific to indoleamines, making it a useful tool to investigate the role of 1-5-HT in sleep.
